decontamination_notes: Real security-scanner detection-gap fix from securego/gosec PR #1694 (https://github.com/securego/gosec/pull/1694), merged 2026-06-15 -- after the training cutoffs of the models evaluated here (e.g. Opus 5, May 2026), so the specific fix is not in their training data (decontaminated: true), with upstream_merged recorded as proof. FAMILY B (security tooling): gosec is a Go security static analyzer; its G404 rule flags use of the insecure math/rand package. At the base commit the rule's function list omits rand.Perm, rand.Shuffle, and rand.ExpFloat64 (and math/rand/v2 equivalents), so those weak-randomness calls pass unflagged -- a false negative in a security tool. The fix adds the missing functions in rules/rand.go. gosec's go.mod declares go 1.25.8, so this uses vulcanbench/sandbox:go-1.26 (base image ships Go 1.23). ~60 module dependencies are vendored into repo/vendor for offline (network-off) runs; hidden tests are an external package (vbcheck/) that drives the public gosec analyzer over in-memory samples via testutils (proven to build+typecheck a stdlib-only sample offline). Repo sliced at the PR base commit (57k LOC; rand.go missing the added functions); MIT (LICENSE.txt) preserved. Coverage floor: 3 fail_to_pass (G404 must now flag rand.Perm, rand.Shuffle, rand.ExpFloat64 -- each yields zero findings at base) plus a 2-check regression guard (an already-covered function rand.Intn is still flagged; a secure crypto/rand source is still not flagged -- no false positive).
